So I've put around 600 miles on my folder so far. I think I've had a fair amount of time to judge it.

It's been great. The hinges are still all working just as perfectly as the day I got it and the feel of the bike remains stiff, which is quite amazing to me. I should note that at 5'9" and 135 pounds, I am fairly light compared to the average person. If I had to guess, I would say that my weight is probably a factor in the hinges holding up so well. I can haul close to 40 pounds of groceries on this little 20" wheel bike because I've taken some extra care in setting it up for that exact purpose, and when I do haul that much, it does change the feel of the bike, and I don't just mean the steering. So I mainly use it for light commuting, small errands, and to haul no more than around 15 pounds of stuff normally, but I still like having the option to carry more on it. The wide tires also make the ride extremely comfortable.

I haven't had to replace a single part on the bike yet. I expect that I won't until I hit close to 1000 miles, at which point I may have to replace the chain, rear cassette, and front chain ring, and possibly the pedals, as the stock ones are all fairly cheap quality. Since the bike itself is extremely solid and well made, and since I got it for such a great price, I can't really complain. I love the little guy.

I also love being able to fold it up and wheel it around with me or put it in a shopping cart. It's an extra piece of mind that you don't get with a normal bike, and it's the main reason I got the bike in the first place. It makes a huge difference when you're not constantly worried about somebody stealing your bike!

So overall, it's been everything I hoped for and just a little bit more. If you're thinking about getting a folding bike for short trips, commuting, or errands, I highly recommend it. Just make sure you do your homework and pick the best bike for you and your price range. Just steer clear of the cheap stuff, because you don't want to skimp too much on price when it comes to a folder. Quality is critical, especially in the welds and hinges. If you do that, you probably won't regret it. I certainly haven't.
